text:
A: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, hello. I can hear you.
A: Oh, good. I'm Agnieszka, I'm in Basingstoke.
B: I'm Annelies. Sheffield.
A: I saw your photo, with the Delft jug. Are you Dutch?
B: Yes, well spotted. From Amersfoort. But I've been here thirty years.
A: Oh, me too, sort of, sorry, not thirty, I'm from Poland. Rzeszów. I came in 2007. So now I'm, you know, from both places, a bit.
B: Yes. I know that feeling quite well.
A: What do you do, if you don't mind?
B: Erm, I'm an executive assistant. For the head of a faculty, at the university.
A: No! I'm also executive assistant! For a CFO, at insurance company. That's so funny.
B: Really? Then you know about board papers.
A: Oh, board papers. I check everything three times. My boss thinks I'm crazy.
B: I think that's just being good at the job. Committee papers are the same. Someone always sends the wrong version at the last minute.
A: Always! At five o'clock, the night before. Do you have team?
B: Two junior administrators. They're lovely. I try to keep things, erm, calm for them. Even when I'm not calm myself.
A: Yes, I understand. Everybody thinks I'm calm. Inside, not always.
B: No. Inside, not always.
A: Do you go back to Holland much?
B: Twice a year. On the ferry, from Hull to Rotterdam. I don't like flying.
A: Oh, I'm so nervous at airports! I'm there three hours early, everything in one folder.
B: The ferry is better for that. You get on in the evening, have a meal, sleep, and you wake up in Rotterdam.
A: That sounds much nicer than Luton, honestly.
B: Most things are nicer than Luton.
A: Ha! True. Is your family still there?
B: My sister, in Utrecht. And my mother. She's, erm, she's not so well now. It's hard being far away.
A: Yes. My parents also, they're getting older. I'm always thinking, if something happens, I'm two hours away, plus airport. Sorry, that's sad thing to talk about.
B: No, it's alright. It's nice to talk to someone who understands it.
A: Yes. Okay, something happier. Do you garden? I saw a bird feeder.
B: A little. Vegetables in the back. And a robin has started coming to the feeder, which I'm very chuffed about.
A: Oh, lovely. My hanging baskets all died in the heatwave. All of them.
B: Mine too, actually. I forgot to water them for one weekend.
A: One weekend, that's all it takes!
B: I think we're almost at time.
